mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate signals a tightening monetary policy cycle, compressing equity discount rates and leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces non-significant negative 20d returns (p>0.05) when FEDFUNDS rise, or in expansion regimes FEDFUNDS rises do not correlate with negative returns.

mechanism_narrative: When demand growth (GDPC1) outpaces supply growth (INDPRO), it signals excess demand, boosting equity valuations and producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 growth > INDPRO growth in the next month
failure_condition: The demand-supply gap reverses or the effect on returns is not statistically significant (p>0.05) when the gap is positive.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in unemployment (UNRATE below 2%) signals a strengthening labor market, boosting consumer confidence and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: UNRATE remains above 2% or S&P 500 returns are not significantly positive (p>0.05) when UNRATE drops below 2%.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary contraction phase (FEDFUNDS > 2.5%), rising interest rates compress equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20d returns are not significantly negative (p>0.05) when FEDFUNDS rise, or in contraction phases the effect is absent.

mechanism_narrative: Rising employment (PAYEMS) coupled with falling unemployment (UNRATE) signals a robust labor market, enhancing corporate performance and driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increase and UNRATE decrease in the same month
failure_condition: The labor market indicators move in tandem but S&P 500 returns are not significantly positive (p>0.05) over the 5-day horizon.

mechanism_narrative: Sustained increases in employment (PAYEMS) reflect a strengthening labor market, boosting consumer spending and corporate profits, which drive positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: PAYEMS rises but S&P 500 returns are not significantly positive (p>0.05) over the 20-day horizon.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in supply growth (INDPRO below 95) indicates reduced production capacity, leading to excess demand and higher equity valuations, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: INDPRO drops below 95 but S&P 500 returns are not significantly positive (p>0.05) over the 60-day horizon, or supply contraction reverses before the period ends.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion with high inflation (GDPC1 >5% and CPIAUCSL >3%), excess demand outpaces supply, leading to market overvaluation and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The late-cycle conditions are met but S&P 500 returns are not significantly negative (p>0.05) over the 5-day horizon, or the effect reverses in subsequent periods.
